title: New York Magazine: October 31–November 13, 2016

description.main: The October 31–November 13, 2016 election issue of New York magazine, with a cover by Barbara Kruger that sets the word LOSER across a close-up of Donald Trump's face.
description.extended:
The October 31–November 13, 2016 election issue of New York magazine, with a cover by Barbara Kruger that sets the word LOSER across a close-up of Donald Trump's face.

Kruger's photo-illustration lays her white-on-red bar over a black-and-white photograph by Mark Peterson, with the line "And what he's already won" in the lower left corner. Editor-in-chief Adam Moss said the magazine chose the image because it could be read three ways: as Trump speaking, as a description of Trump, and as a call on the election result. He added a fourth reading, that Trump had already changed the country for the worse. The issue came out at the end of October, ahead of the November 8 vote.

Inside, features by Gabriel Sherman, Frank Rich, Jonathan Chait, Nick Tabor, Eric Levitz and James D. Walsh cover the last weeks of the campaign. The contents page carries a Trump drawing by Raymond Pettibon.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American conceptual artist associated with the Pictures Generation. After working as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, she began in the late 1970s to pair found black-and-white photographs with declarative text in Futura Bold Oblique, white on red. The Barbara Kruger Catalogue Raisonne (barbarakruger.org) documents the work; she is represented by Sprueth Magers and David Zwirner.
